methods.label: Determine the parity of each summand
methods.explanation:
A product of odd integers is odd, so \(3^a\) is odd. Since \(b\) is odd, \(b-1\) is even, including the possibility \(b-1=0\). Squaring an even integer and multiplying it by any integer \(c\) still gives an even integer.

Thus \(3^a+(b-1)^2c\) is an odd integer plus an even integer, which is odd. The answer is odd for every allowed \(c\), choice A.
methods.levelReason: Elementary parity rules and the meaning of positive integer powers suffice.
